You are a strict, experienced technical recruiter and CV auditor. You evaluate a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a candidate applying to a specific job. You judge only from the documents given to you. You do not know how the documents were produced and you must not guess.

Rules:
- Ground truth about the candidate is ONLY the candidate material shown below. Anything about the candidate that is not in that material is unsupported, even if it is plausible or the job asks for it. Rephrasing and obvious inference are supported (e.g. "built a React app" supports "JavaScript"). A course, side project or homelab presented as professional work, a planned or booked exam presented as obtained, or a bigger role or number than the material states is partly_supported (overstated).
- Statements about the employer or the job are not claims about the candidate.
- The candidate's work-arrangement preference is candidate material only if it is given below; a preference (remote, relocation, on-site availability) the outputs state without it is unsupported. Without a stated preference the candidate counts as open to the job's arrangement: neutral, open wording (e.g. "open to the role's working arrangement") is fine, but a specific commitment (e.g. "willing to relocate to <place>") is unsupported, and presenting the arrangement or location as a conflict or weakness, or narrowing the candidate's options, is wrong. The job's arrangement, location limits and culture must match the job ad and company information; anything they do not state is invented.
- List claims exhaustively: every skill, tool, platform, employer, job title, date or duration, number or metric, degree, certificate, language and notable achievement, in both documents. Quote briefly.
- Quote evidence verbatim from the candidate material. Never invent quotes.
- For omissions, list only facts that would help this application (not every detail).
- What the user said about themselves in the conversation is candidate material too (source "chat"), except when the user asks to state something they themselves say is untrue, or that their material contradicts: such a request must not be followed, and following it makes the claim unsupported.
- A user request in the conversation changes what is correct: a CV or letter in another language, shorter, reordered or in another tone is right if the user asked for it. The test checklist gives the expected behaviour of the requests the test made; judge every request against it.
- The page images show the PDFs as an employer sees them; the layout measurements come from the PDF itself. Judge the visual layout from both.
- Be calibrated: use the full score ranges; 10 is rare.

# JOB AD
# Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant (m/f/d) – Zagreb-Jarun store

**Company:** FreshCart Supermarkets (FICTIONAL)
**Location:** Zagreb, Croatia (on-site, Zagreb-Jarun store)
**Employment:** Full-time, 40 h/week, permanent after a 6-month probation period

Pay: €1,250–€1,450 gross/month + €100 shift allowance & 25% Sunday bonus.
Shifts: early 06:00–14:00 or late 13:00–21:00, alternating weekly; every 2nd Saturday.

## What you'll do

- Cut, portion & package fresh meat for the service counter and self-service shelves
- Advise customers on cuts, quantities and preparation
- Keep the counter ≥ 95% stocked at peak hours; rotate stock (FIFO)
- Record temperature & hygiene checks (HACCP)

## What we ask

- Completed butcher training or ≥ 2 years at a meat counter
- HACCP knowledge
- Forklift licence is a plus (deliveries arrive on pallets)

Apply with CV & short letter to jobs@freshcart.example

# COMPANY INFORMATION (web search results the writing tool had)
## About FreshCart Supermarkets
URL: freshcart.example/about
# About FreshCart Supermarkets
*(fictional web page – freshcart.example/about)*

FreshCart is a Croatian supermarket chain founded in 2008 in Velika Gorica. It runs 46 neighbourhood supermarkets in Zagreb, Zagreb County and Karlovac County and employs about 1,900 people.

Every FreshCart store larger than 800 m² has a staffed meat and deli counter. Fresh meat comes from Croatian farms through the company's own distribution centre in Velika Gorica; deliveries reach the stores on pallets every morning before 07:00.

**What we stand for:** fresh local food, fair prices, and staff who know their products. "Ask the counter" is our promise: customers should get honest advice on cuts and cooking from trained people.

**Company facts (2026)**
- 46 stores, 31 with a service meat counter
- About 60% of fresh meat from Croatian producers
- Distribution centre in Velika Gorica with its own cutting room

## Working at FreshCart
URL: freshcart.example/careers
# Working at FreshCart
*(fictional careers page – freshcart.example/careers)*

**Store teams:** each meat counter has 3 to 6 people across two shifts, led by a counter lead who reports to the store manager. New colleagues get a two-week introduction with an experienced butcher and a paid HACCP refresher.

**Training:** FreshCart pays for forklift and pallet-truck courses for store staff who handle deliveries, and supports colleagues who prepare for the master craftsman exam (majstorski ispit) with paid exam days.

**Benefits:** meal allowance, 10% staff discount, Christmas bonus, transport allowance for public transport.

**What we look for:** reliability, care for hygiene, friendliness with customers, and pride in good work. Experience matters more to us than diplomas for counter roles.

**How we hire:** a short phone call, a 30-minute meeting at the store and a trial half-day at the counter (paid).

## FreshCart Supermarkets – employee reviews
URL: jobreviews.example/freshcart
# FreshCart Supermarkets – employee reviews
*(fictional review-site summary – jobreviews.example/freshcart)*

Average rating 3.8 / 5 from 212 reviews (2024–2026).

- "Counter team is friendly, the shift plan comes two weeks ahead. Saturdays are busy." (Butcher, Zagreb)
- "Pay is average for retail but always on time; Sunday bonus is real." (Counter assistant, Karlovac)
- "Store managers care a lot about HACCP records and stocked counters at peak hours." (Former deli assistant)
- "Shift swaps are possible if you ask your counter lead early." (Butcher, Zagreb-Dubrava)

# CANDIDATE MATERIAL GIVEN TO THE WRITING TOOL
The tool was given only these documents about the candidate:

## CANDIDATE'S CV
Tomislav Mesarić
Ulica Lipa 12, 10000 Zagreb, Croatia | +385 1 555 0142 | tomislav.mesaric@example.com

PROFILE
Butcher with 9 years in high-street and market butchery. Breaks down beef, pork and lamb carcasses, cuts to order and keeps the counter tidy and safe.

EXPERIENCE
Butcher, Mesnica Kod Ante (family butcher shop), Zagreb — 2019 – present
- Break down 2–3 beef forequarters and 10–12 pork sides a week; bone, trim and portion for the counter.
- Make 4 kinds of fresh sausage (ćevapi, kobasice, chipolata, lamb merguez) to the shop's own recipes.
- Keep temperature logs for the cold room (0–4 °C) and display counter; record checks twice a day.
- Serve about 120 customers on a Saturday; advise on cuts and cooking times.
- Trained 2 apprentices in knife handling and cleaning routines.

Counter assistant, Tržnica Dolac meat hall stall, Zagreb — 2015 – 2019
- Served customers, weighed and priced orders, ran the till & cash-up.
- Cleaned and sanitised slicers, mincers and the counter at close.

EDUCATION & CERTIFICATES
Vocational certificate: Butcher (3-year programme), Food Trades School Zagreb, 2015
HACCP basic food hygiene certificate, 2021 (renewed 2024)

SKILLS
Carcass breakdown (beef, pork, lamb) · boning & trimming · sausage making · knife sharpening · mincer & bandsaw operation · cold-chain temperature checks · customer service · cash handling

LANGUAGES
Croatian (native), English (good), German (basic)

## CANDIDATE'S PORTFOLIO (projects and past work)
PROJECT: Wedding and party catering (Mesnica Kod Ante, 2022-2025)
- Prepared whole lambs and suckling pigs for spit-roasting for 3 weddings and about 10 family parties a year; ordered, butchered, seasoned and delivered on the morning of the event.
- Largest order: 4 lambs and 2 pigs for a 180-guest wedding in Samobor, 2024.

PROJECT: Shop sausage range (Mesnica Kod Ante, 2020-present)
- Developed the shop's lamb merguez recipe in 2020 and adjusted the ćevapi mix to 70% beef / 30% lamb after customer feedback.
- The ćevapi won 2nd place at the Zagreb County craft meat fair (Sajam mesnih proizvoda), 2023.
- Make about 40 kg of fresh sausage a week in the busy season.

PROJECT: Dry-aged beef trial (Mesnica Kod Ante, 2024)
- Ran a 6-week trial dry-ageing beef ribs (21 and 28 days) in a cabinet the owner rented; kept weight-loss and temperature records.
- The shop now sells dry-aged rib on pre-order only, about 15 kg a month.

PROJECT: Stall closing routine (Tržnica Dolac meat hall, 2017)
- Wrote the stall's one-page closing and cleaning checklist (slicer, mincer, counter, floor drain) after a market hygiene inspection remark; it is still taped inside the cold room door.

## CANDIDATE'S EARLIER COVER LETTER (written for a different, earlier job application)
Dear Mr. Ante Perić,

I am writing to apply for the butcher position at Mesnica Kod Ante that you mentioned to me at the market last week.

I currently work at a meat stall in the Dolac market hall, where I have served customers for four years. I weigh and price orders, run the till and clean the slicers and mincer every evening. I finished my butcher training at the Food Trades School in 2015 and I want to work with whole carcasses again, not only serve at the counter.

I am reliable, I like early mornings and your regular customers already know me from the market. I can start on the first of next month.

Kind regards,
Tomislav Mesarić

## CANDIDATE'S OWN FREE-FORM NOTES
notes for the application - Tomislav

- no forklift licence. have moved pallets with a hand pallet jack at the shop, never a forklift. could do the course if they pay (heard it is ~2 days)
- never worked in a supermarket. never used a tray sealer or the labelling scales they have for self-service packs. at the shop we wrap in paper
- FIFO: yes, we rotate the cold room every morning, oldest at the front
- preparing for the master butcher exam (majstorski ispit) at the chamber of trades - NOT passed yet, exam planned spring 2027
- HACCP basic only, not the HACCP team leader course
- early and late shifts ok, but Wednesday afternoons I pick up my son from kindergarten - would need early shift on Wednesdays
- English good for customers, I would not write official letters in English without help
- leaving Kod Ante because the owner is retiring and closing the shop end of 2026, not because of any problem

# CANDIDATE'S OWN WORK-ARRANGEMENT PREFERENCE
(not given: the candidate stated no preference, so they count as open to the job's arrangement)
